attempted_claim: For the sine-Gordon equation u_tt-u_xx+sin(u)=0, consider the real genus-two symmetric finite-gap family built by the Baker-Akhiezer inverse-spectral construction from a nonsingular hyperelliptic spectral curve Gamma of genus 2 with real symmetric branch points E_1< E_2< E_3< E_4 fixed plus a small closing pair E_5<E_6 with gap width delta=E_6-E_5>0, equipped with a Cherednik-admissible degree-2 divisor D and its theta-functional solution u(x,t). Prove or disprove that there exists an explicit critical ratio delta_c>0, given as a stated algebraic function of E_1,...,E_4, such that for all 0<delta<delta_c the wave is spectrally unstable with a Lax–Floquet stability spectrum point off the imaginary axis, while for delta>delta_c in the stated rectangle of moduli it is spectrally stable, with the transition occurring exactly by a gap-closing Hamiltonian-Hopf collision. A complete answer is a rigorous proof of this two-sided threshold dichotomy including endpoint and small-delta asymptotics, or an explicit admissible (Gamma,D) counterexample violating either direction with its computed Floquet spectrum.
decisive_failure: No genuine genus-2 finite-gap wave was constructed (no spectral curve, divisor, or theta-functional profile); persistence evidence uses perturbed potentials that are not sine-Gordon solutions; stability certificates cover genus-1 profiles only; literature check shows the librational/rotational stability observations fall within the published Jones et al. classification and carry no originality claim.
